title: hosted-api-long-tail-queue-saturation-and-safe-async-fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a major customer escalation, we observed sustained 5xx/timeouts on the Hosted API driven by long-tail queue saturation in the fronting proxy and request fanout to model backends. Client SDK retries and aggressive on-prem tenant bursts amplified latency and produced retry storms that pushed the proxy beyond its soft queueing limits. This ticket tracks the engineering investigation, immediate mitigations, and planned engineering fixes to prevent recurrence.
impact: High customer-visible errors for 3 large tenants leading to degraded throughput and elevated 5xx rates for ~45 minutes. Some customers reported client-level repeated failures and manual retry loops prolonged recovery.
reproduction_steps: Simulate burst from single tenant with >500 concurrent short-lived requests (seq length 256) and SDK configured with aggressive immediate retries (0ms backoff, 3 retries).
Route through proxy with limited request-queue depth (config used in prod can be toggled in staging).
Introduce transient backend slowing (add 250ms per-request artificial delay on model pool) to create head-of-line blocking.
Observe proxy queue depth growth, queued request TTL expirations, and notable increase in 502/504 responses and client-triggered retries.
root_cause_summary: A confluence of factors: (1) proxy request queueing behavior allows long queues without early fast-fail for tail latency risk, (2) client SDK default retry semantics do not respect idempotency signals and retry immediately, (3) model backend transient slowdown increased service times which interacted poorly with continuous batching, (4) no tenant-scoped concurrent request caps upstream, enabling a single tenant to occupy queue capacity and starve others.
immediate_mitigations_executed: Applied tenant-level emergency request-rate limit (per-tenant QPS cap) for affected tenants via control plane at 2025-01-10T16:12Z.
Rolled temporary proxy config to reduce queue depth from 1000->200 and enable 100ms soft-queue fast-fail threshold at 2025-01-10T16:25Z.
Notified SDK teams and published guidance to clients to adopt exponential backoff and idempotency tokens; special customer comms sent to impacted accounts.
Activated model-variant fallback policy for one affected tenant to downgrade to a lower-latency quantized variant until throughput normalized.
timeline: 2025-01-10T15:40Z - First customer escalation opened reporting increased 5xx and timeouts.
2025-01-10T15:52Z - Correlated spikes on proxy queue depth and per-tenant request concurrency in observability dashboards.
2025-01-10T16:05Z - Identified SDK immediate-retry pattern on samples from customer logs.
2025-01-10T16:12Z - Emergency tenant QPS cap applied (temporary mitigation).
2025-01-10T16:25Z - Proxy config rolled to reduce soft queue depth and enable early fast-fail; 5xx rates start to decline.
2025-01-10T16:50Z - Full traffic normalization for most tenants; continued monitoring and root cause analysis begins.
proposed_fixes: Implement tenant-scoped soft concurrency windows in proxy with graceful fast-fail when tail latency risk threshold exceeded.

Introduce an async fallback path: when queued time > X ms, return a fast lightweight response that triggers async processing + webhook/websocket notification to avoid client-side retries and reduce blocking.
Update SDKs to respect 'x-request-idempotency' header and adopt jittered exponential backoff default retries; add versioned SDK release and migration notes.
Align proxy and runtime idle/queue TTLs so queued requests expire before backend timeouts and generate clear retryable vs non-retryable error codes.
Add tenant-priority metrics and automated cooling rules that proactively limit QPS from a single tenant when head-of-line risk detected.
acceptance_criteria: New proxy config prevents long-tail queue growth in staging under reproduced load test (no more than 5% of requests exceed 95th percentile latency threshold).
SDK default retry policy updated and released (>=1 patch release) with docs and migration guidance; customer SDKs consume new default within 30 days.
Async fallback implemented and tested for correctness and observability; system emits a clear 'degraded-async-fallback' metric for each occurrence.
No regression in throughput or tail-latency for healthy tenants after tenant-scoped limits enabled (verified via canary rollout).
implementation_notes: We will coordinate a staged rollout: proxy change -> canary on 10% traffic -> observe 24h -> expand. Async fallback requires a small API extension; design doc attached. SDK changes should be backwards compatible; we will ensure idempotency header is optional but recommended.

notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on eliminating long-tail queueing as a root cause of retry amplification. Related tenant-shaping and global circuit breaker work is referenced in follow-ups. Postmortem will be published after deploy and 2-week observation window.
